neighbours.label: the colon after a language name that introduces a foreign-language gloss, e.g. '(Greek: ...)', '(Hebrew: ...)'
fire: The Roman province of Asia (Greek: Ἀσία) lay on the western coast.
The synagogue was called Kahal Kadosh (Hebrew: Holy Congregation) by its founders.
The festival of lights (Sanskrit: दीपावली) is celebrated in autumn.
The old fortress (Arabic: القلعة) overlooks the harbour.
His motto was carpe diem (Latin: seize the day) for most of his life.
The capital of the region (German: Hauptstadt) moved twice in a century.
The ancient city of Ephesus (Turkish: Efes) attracts many visitors.
The word for soul (Greek: ψυχή) appears often in his letters.
quiet: The Roman province of Asia (now western Turkey) lay on the western coast.
The synagogue was called Kahal Kadosh (founded 1654) by its founders.
The festival of lights (held each year) is celebrated in autumn.
The old fortress (built in 1520) overlooks the harbour.
His motto was to seize the day (as he often said) for most of his life.
The capital of the region (see map) moved twice in a century.
The ancient city of Ephesus (near Selçuk) attracts many visitors.
The word for soul (see chapter two) appears often in his letters.
